title: Machine learning enriched MthUPO variants for beta-damascone hydroxylation
summary: Researchers combined experimental activity measurements with machine learning to enrich a second MthUPO peroxygenase library for substrate-specific activity. Across 506 distinct variants screened and sequenced, 97 of 108 variants in the ML-enriched library outperformed wild type in the screening assay, compared with 14% in the initial htFuncLib library. The authors report an 11.8-fold turnover number for the best variant producing 4-hydroxy-beta-damascone, with greater than 99% regioisomeric excess. Separate 5–12-fold enrichment and recovery figures in the paper are simulation benchmarks and are not treated as experimental outcomes.
ai_technology: Machine-learning enrichment of experimental enzyme-activity data following htFuncLib design

source_review.scope: Official bioRxiv API v1 metadata/abstract and primary indexed v1 full-text excerpts; simulation and experimental results kept separate.

evidence.tested: The preprint reports screening and sequencing 506 distinct MthUPO variants. In the ML-enriched library, 97 of 108 variants outperformed wild type in the screening assay, compared with 14% in the initial htFuncLib library. The best reported variant had an 11.8-fold turnover number for 4-hydroxy-beta-damascone with greater than 99% regioisomeric excess.
evidence.unknown: The preprint is not peer reviewed. The paper separately reports simulation-only MLEE/htFuncLib comparisons, which are excluded from the experimental result summary. Assay outcomes do not establish process-scale productivity or commercial suitability.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning used experimental enzyme-activity measurements to enrich a library of MthUPO variants for testing, following an earlier htFuncLib design stage.
